name: Layout: move annotation panel to sidenotes gutter
steps: Move the step annotation text (title, description, shape) from the right panel inside the figure card to the sidenotes gutter/column alongside the figure
The full card width is now available for the visualization — remove the internal two-column grid split
Annotation text should update on each step change, same as before, just rendered in the sidenote margin
Verify annotations are readable and properly positioned in both dark and light themes
On mobile (where sidenotes collapse inline), annotations should appear below the viz area
Update step counter display to work with the new layout
Verify no build errors with pnpm build

name: Renumber steps from 12 to 14 and update infrastructure
steps: Old step 6 splits into new steps 6 (embeddings matrix) and 7 (layer norm + QKV) — add placeholder for new step 6
New step 12 is an attention heatmap inserted after QK^T — add placeholder

New step mapping: 1 Black Box, 2 Tokenize, 3 Embeddings, 4 Positional, 5 Combine, 6 Embeddings Matrix, 7 Layer Norm + QKV, 8 Q Projection, 9 V Projection, 10 K + Transpose, 11 QK^T Scores, 12 Attention Heatmap, 13 Attn × V, 14 Residual/Output
Update STEP_DATA array with 14 entries (new entries 6 and 12 can have placeholder text for now)
Update step counter to show 'Step N / 14'
Update forward/back button disable logic for 14 steps
Renumber all renderStepN() dispatch calls to match new numbering
Verify existing visualizations still render at their new step numbers
Verify no build errors with pnpm build

name: Step 1 redesign: horizontal sentence with black box
steps: Present the input as a natural horizontal sentence: 'The fat cat sat quietly on the ___' — NOT as separate word chips in boxes
Make it visually clear this is an incomplete sentence and the model must predict the next word (use a blank/underscore or trailing cursor)
Keep the black box ('Transformer ?') and 'mat' prediction, but flow is now: horizontal sentence → arrow → black box → arrow → 'mat'
Remove 'Input → [Transformer] → Output' from the annotation shape text
The sentence text must persist into Step 2 for visual continuity — do NOT destroy it on step change
Verify clean rendering at desktop and mobile widths in both themes

name: Step 2 redesign: animate text into tokens with visual continuity
steps: On transition from Step 1 → Step 2: wipe the black box and prediction elements, but KEEP the horizontal sentence text from Step 1
Animate the sentence text separating into individual token chips in place — words spread apart and colored token borders/backgrounds appear around them
'quietly' splits into 'quiet' + 'ly' with subword color coding (amber), other tokens get whole-word color (blue), matching section 03
Show token count below
The token chips must persist into Step 3 — visual continuity means the same DOM elements carry forward
Verify the forward AND backward transitions are smooth (Step 2 → Step 1 should reverse the animation or re-render Step 1 cleanly)

name: Step 3 redesign: column pills with visual continuity
steps: On transition from Step 2 → Step 3: keep the token chips, animate them upward to make room below
Add horizontal spacing between tokens to accommodate embedding columns
Animate embedding vectors expanding downward beneath each token as unified column pills (one rounded rectangle per token, NOT separate cells)
Each column pill has internal row separators showing sample numeric values, with a horizontal ellipsis (⋯) in the MIDDLE row (pandas-style truncation, not at the bottom)
Columns are colored blue (token embedding color)
Add d_model as a y-axis label on the left side of the columns — remove any '8 tokens × d_model' bottom label
The embedding annotation card at the bottom (vocab lookup explanation) should be permanent for this step — remove the × close button
Verify column pills are visually cohesive and emphasize one-vector-per-token

name: Step 4 redesign: positional embeddings with visual continuity
steps: On transition from Step 3 → Step 4: keep token chips and blue column pills in place — do NOT remove and redraw
Animate blue columns shrinking in width to make room; fade out or visually de-emphasize internal numbers (numbers don't aid comprehension here)
Animate yellow positional embedding column pills expanding beside each blue column
Fix horizontal alignment: token chips, down arrows, and column pairs must be centered on the same vertical axis per token
Remove '8 tokens × 2 embeddings × d_model' label text
Verify alignment is correct and columns don't clip at right edge on standard viewport widths

name: Step 5 redesign: per-token merge animation with alignment
steps: On transition from Step 4 → Step 5: each blue+yellow column pair merges into a single green column
Critical: each pair collapses inward UNDER ITS OWN TOKEN — not toward the center of the card
The green merged column should be centered directly under its token chip and down arrow
Fix any horizontal misalignment between tokens, arrows, and columns
Remove '8 tokens × d_model' label text
The sidenote about combination methods should remain
Green columns must persist into Step 6 for visual continuity

name: New Step 6: embeddings matrix formation (split from old step 6)
steps: On transition from Step 5 → Step 6: the separate green column pills consolidate into a single cohesive matrix visualization
This should be visually continuous — the green columns slide together and a matrix border/grid appears around them
Matrix has token labels as column headers, d_model as row axis with horizontal ellipsis (⋯) in the middle row
Sample numeric values appear in cells (green-tinted, representing combined embeddings)
This step is purely about forming the matrix object — no normalization or QKV yet
Annotation text should explain: we now have a matrix where each column is one token's combined embedding vector

name: New Step 7: layer norm + QKV weights (split from old step 6)
steps: On transition from Step 6 → Step 7: animate normalization — swap cell values and shift tint from green to purple
After normalization animation, QKV weight matrices appear below
Critical: QKV weight cards must have the SAME visual style as the feature matrix — same column pill structure, same ellipsis placement, same cell sizing
W_Q (blue), W_K (orange), W_V (pink) — each shows d_model × d_head with correct dimensions
The visual match between input matrix and weight matrices should make it intuitively clear they are compatible for multiplication
Annotation explains layer normalization and introduces the three learned projection weights

name: Step 8 redesign: Q projection with per-token animation
steps: Animate W_Q moving up from its position to a multiplication area beside the input matrix
Draw an empty Q output matrix (correct size: T × d_head) with token labels but no values yet

For each token column in the input matrix: (1) draw a highlight box around the column, (2) animate a 'copy' of that column to W_Q, (3) signal multiplication, (4) animate the result into the corresponding column of the Q output matrix
The per-token animation can be fast (don't need to watch all 8 slowly) — maybe animate 1-2 tokens fully, then fill remaining columns quickly
Annotation text: query vectors represent 'what am I looking for?' — each token's embedding is projected into query space
Q matrix and input matrix must persist for the next step

name: Step 9 redesign: V projection with stacked card effect
steps: On transition: move W_Q back to its starting position, move W_V to the multiplication area
Move the completed Q matrix backward in the visual stack — shrink slightly and dim it (opacity ~0.5)
Draw the V output matrix in the same position where Q was (front of the stack), creating a 'stacked card' effect
Run the same per-token copy/multiply/drag animation as Step 8 but with W_V and pink coloring
Both Q (dimmed, behind) and V (active, front) should be visible, showing accumulation of projections
Annotation text: value vectors represent 'what information do I carry?'

name: Step 10 redesign: K projection with animated transpose
steps: Clear the Q/V card stack to make room
Run the same per-token projection animation for W_K (orange), producing K matrix (T × d_head)
Critical transpose animation: each column of K visually rotates to become a row of K^T — the dimension flip from (T × d_head) to (d_head × T) must be unmistakable
Token labels should move from column headers to row labels during the transpose
Show dimension labels changing during the rotation
Annotation text: explain that K^T flips rows ↔ columns so the inner dimensions (d_head) will align for multiplication with Q
Also explain WHY K comes last: the transpose is essential for understanding how parallelized attention works

name: Step 11 redesign: QK^T with correct matrix sizes
steps: Show Q (T × d_head) and K^T (d_head × T) at their actual proportional sizes — Q is tall, K^T is wide
Animate d_head inner dimension cancellation with strikethrough
Animate the dot product producing the T × T attention scores matrix — if feasible, animate row-by-row (row i of Q against all columns of K^T)
Result is a T × T matrix with token labels on both axes (queries on rows, keys on columns)
Keep the O(n²) callout
Enrich annotation: explain that element (i,j) is the dot product of token i's query with token j's key — all T² pairwise similarities computed at once
The T × T matrix must persist for the next step (attention heatmap)

name: New Step 12: interactive attention heatmap (from section 04c)
steps: Zoom into the T × T attention scores matrix from Step 11, expanding it to fill the viz area
Render it as the interactive attention heatmap currently in section 04c — with click/hover to highlight rows and columns, tooltip showing score values
Preserve the same interactivity and visual polish from 04c (color scale, token labels on both axes)
Add softmax explanation: note that raw scores are passed through softmax to produce normalized attention weights (rows sum to 1)
After this feature is verified, REMOVE the heatmap from section 04c (it now lives here in the walkthrough)
Annotation text: this is the attention pattern — each row shows how much one token attends to every other token

name: Step 13 redesign: Attention × V with clearer dimensions
steps: Show attention weights matrix (T × T) multiplied by V (T × d_head) producing output (T × d_head)
Matrices must be drawn at proportional sizes that make the dimensions visually intuitive — T × T is square, V is tall-and-narrow, output is tall-and-narrow
Animate T inner dimension cancellation with strikethrough
Add softmax context: note that the attention weights used here are the softmax-normalized values from the previous step
Annotation text: each output row is a weighted blend of value vectors, dimensionality is restored from T × T back to T × d_head
Verify dimension labels and matrix sizing make the operation visually self-explanatory

name: Step 14 redesign: attention head output (clearer ending)
steps: Reframe this step to clearly signal 'this is the output of one attention head'
Show the residual connection (input + attention output) but label it more accessibly — avoid jargon like 'enriched' that is opaque to non-experts
Use language like 'Head Output' or 'Attention Result' rather than 'Residual Connection' as the primary framing
Keep the feed-forward network preview but make it clearly non-interactive (dim or dashed styling so it doesn't look clickable)
Annotation text: this is what one attention head produces — the output is added back to the input (residual connection) and feeds forward to the next layer
The figure should end with a sense of completion — this attention head's job is done

name: Object continuity for steps 3–5: token chips + embedding columns
steps: Create a persistent layer spanning steps 3–5 containing: 8 token chips (small, step-3 style), 8 down arrows, and 8 blue embedding pill columns
Step 3 shows all persistent elements at full opacity. Step-extras: y-axis label, pill grid values, sidenote
Step 3→4: token chips and blue pills persist in DOM. Blue pills shrink in width (CSS transition). Yellow positional pills and legend appear as volatile step-extras
Step 4→5: blue + yellow pill pairs persist. Volatile step-extras: green merged column, merge equation, sidenote. The merge animation collapses pairs into green under each token
FLIP animation on all persistent elements so positional shifts from step-extras height changes are smooth glides, not teleports
Backward navigation (5→4→3) reverse-animates: green splits back into blue+yellow, yellow collapses, pills grow back to step-3 size
Boundary transitions: step 2→3 inserts the persistent layer fresh (no FLIP needed). Step 5→6 destroys it (full rebuild for step 6)
Verify both themes, mobile width, and that step-specific content (sidenote, legend, equation) fades in/out properly

name: Object continuity for steps 5→6: green columns consolidate into matrix
steps: The 8 separate green column pills from step 5 should slide together into a unified matrix grid in step 6, not be destroyed and recreated
Persistent elements: 8 green column bodies (pill shapes), token labels above each column, d_model y-axis label
Step 5→6 transition: columns glide horizontally toward each other (gap shrinks), a matrix border/outline fades in around them, cell values (previously hidden or faded) become visible
Step 6→5 backward: matrix border fades out, columns spread apart, values fade, restoring the step-5 separated-pill look
FLIP animation handles the horizontal position changes of each column pill as gap collapses
Token labels FLIP from their step-5 positions (above separated pills) to step-6 positions (column headers in matrix)
Verify the consolidation animation looks like the columns are physically merging into a single object

name: Object continuity for steps 6→7: matrix normalization
steps: The matrix frame, token labels, y-axis label, and column structure from step 6 persist into step 7 — not destroyed and rebuilt
Persistent elements: matrix wrapper (border/outline), 8 column containers, 8 token column-header labels, d_model y-axis label
Step 6→7 transition: cell values animate from green text to purple text, background tint shifts green→purple via CSS transition on the persistent container class
QKV weight matrices (W_Q, W_K, W_V) appear below as volatile step-extras with fade-in animation
Step 7→6 backward: purple→green color transition reverses, QKV weights fade out
FLIP handles any vertical shift of the matrix caused by QKV weights appearing/disappearing below
Unify the CSS class names between step 6 (hw-mat6-*) and step 7 (hw-norm7-*) so the same DOM elements can be reused

name: Object continuity for steps 8–10: input matrix across Q/V/K projections
steps: The normalized input matrix X̂ (T×d_model, purple) and its token labels are identical across steps 8, 9, and 10 — persist them as a single layer
Persistent elements: input matrix wrapper, 8 input column pills, 8 token labels, X̂ label, T×d_model dimension label, dot operator
Step 8: volatile content = W_Q weight matrix, arrow operator, Q output matrix (blue). Per-token animation runs on volatile elements only
Step 8→9: input matrix stays put. W_Q swaps to W_V (volatile rebuild). Q output moves to ghost/stack position, V output appears in front. FLIP animates the input matrix if its position shifts
Step 9→10: input matrix stays put. W_V swaps to W_K (volatile rebuild). Q/V stack clears, K output + transpose section appear as volatile content
Backward navigation reverses: volatile content swaps back, input matrix FLIPs to any new position
Steps 8-10 currently all use hw-q8-* classes for the input — reuse the same DOM nodes directly
Boundary: step 7→8 inserts the persistent layer fresh. Step 10→11 destroys it (step 11 has completely different layout)

name: Object continuity for steps 10→11: K^T persists into QK^T
steps: The K^T matrix visualization from step 10's transpose section should persist as the K^T operand in step 11's QK^T multiplication
Persistent elements: K^T matrix wrapper, K^T label, d_head×T dimension label, token row labels, K^T cell grid
Step 10→11 transition: K^T slides/scales from its step-10 position (below K) to its step-11 position (right side of multiplication row). FLIP animates this movement
Step 10's input matrix, W_K, K output, and transpose arrow are destroyed. Step 11's Q matrix, dot operator, down arrow, and result matrix appear as volatile step-extras
Step 11→10 backward: K^T FLIPs back to its step-10 position, step 10's full layout rebuilds around it
The K^T DOM structure must be compatible between steps — unify hw-k10-kt-* and hw-qkt-kt-* class names or adopt the element with class swapping
Verify the K^T movement animation makes it visually clear the same object is being reused

name: Object continuity for steps 11→12: scores matrix zooms into heatmap
steps: The T×T attention scores matrix from step 11's result section should zoom/expand into step 12's interactive heatmap — not be destroyed and recreated
Persistent elements: 8×8 grid of score cells, query token row labels (left), key token column labels (top)

Step 11→12 transition: the scores grid scales up and repositions to fill the viz area. Cell backgrounds transition from the step-11 fill color to the heatmap color scale. Softmax banner fades in above. Interactive hover behavior activates
Step 12→11 backward: heatmap shrinks back into the scores matrix position, color scale reverses to step-11 styling, hover behavior deactivates, QK^T multiplication elements reappear
FLIP handles the scale + position change of the entire grid and each label
Token labels on both axes must FLIP from their step-11 positions (small, inside result section) to step-12 positions (larger, heatmap axes)
This is the most visually dramatic continuity transition — the matrix physically grows into the heatmap

name: Object continuity for steps 13→14: attention output carries forward
steps: The green attention output matrix (T×d_head) from step 13 should persist as the Attn(x) operand in step 14's residual addition
Persistent elements: output matrix wrapper, 3 output column pills, output cell values, T×d_head dimension label

Step 13→14 transition: the attention matrix and V matrix fade out (destroyed). The green output matrix FLIPs from step 13's '= Output' position to step 14's 'Attn(x)' position. Input matrix and '+' operator appear as volatile step-extras
Step 14→13 backward: green output FLIPs back, step 13's multiplication layout rebuilds around it
Class names differ (hw-av13-out-* vs hw-ho14-attn-*) — either unify them or swap classes on the persistent elements during transition
The output label should transition from 'Output' to 'Attn(x)' (text content update, not DOM replacement)
Verify the green output visually 'carries forward' and the user perceives it as the same object moving to a new context

name: Smooth Step 1↔2 — black box fade + token separation
steps: Both steps share flipBuildSentence() with tok-0..7 flip IDs, so words already match across the transition

Black box, arrow, and prediction elements (in r.extras) snap-disappear on 1→2 — add a GSAP fade-out tween (opacity 1→0, duration 300ms) that runs BEFORE the Flip rebuild, or use onLeave with longer duration

Token spacing goes from continuous sentence to separated chips instantly — Flip handles position but the colored chip backgrounds (appearing on step 2) need a post-Flip tween from transparent/no-background to colored background
After Flip.from() completes for 1→2, tween each tok-0..7 chip's background-color from transparent to the token color, and border from none to the chip border style, over 400ms with per-token stagger
For backward 2→1: reverse the effect — tween chip backgrounds to transparent before or during Flip, and fade-in the black box / arrow / prediction extras via onEnter
Verify rapid clicking (1→2→1→2) doesn't leave artifacts from interrupted tweens — use gsap.killTweensOf() on the relevant elements at the start of each transition
Test in both dark and light themes

name: Smooth Step 2↔3 — tokens persist into columns
steps: tok-0..7 matches across flipBuildSentence() → flipBuildColumns(), but tokens go from inline sentence spans to block column-header chips with very different geometry — ensure Flip animates this position/size change smoothly (may need duration 0.6-0.8s for this boundary)

Embedding columns (blue pills), down arrows, and y-axis label appear all at once via onEnter — add stagger by token index (stagger: 0.04) so columns cascade left-to-right instead of popping in simultaneously
Blue pills should animate height from 0 to full (growing downward under each token) — set initial scaleY(0) with transformOrigin 'top center' in onEnter, tween to scaleY(1)
Down arrows between token chips and blue pills should fade in before the pills grow (sequence: arrows fade in → pills grow downward)
For backward 3→2: columns should shrink upward (scaleY → 0) and arrows fade out before tokens Flip back to sentence positions
The sidenote in step 3 extras should fade in after the column entrance animation completes, not simultaneously
Verify the transition feels like 'tokens dropping into place and columns growing beneath them' rather than an instant layout swap

name: Smooth Step 3↔4↔5 — embedding transitions within columns range
steps: All three steps use flipBuildColumns() with matching flip IDs — since DOM is rebuilt each step, CSS-driven transitions don't fire and need GSAP tweens instead

3→4: After Flip, tween blue pill width from full to narrow over 400ms. Yellow pills enter via onEnter with staggered fade-in (stagger: 0.03) plus scaleY grow from 0 (transformOrigin 'top center') — not instant pop

4→5: Blue+yellow pairs must animate to green merged pill. Set green pills to opacity:0 initially, after Flip tween green to opacity:1 while simultaneously tweening blue+yellow to opacity:0, over 500ms. No intermediate 'washed out' ghost state where all three are partially visible
For backward 5→4: green pill fades to 0, blue+yellow fade from 0 to 1 (reverse of merge). 4→3: yellow pills shrink (scaleY→0) and fade out, blue pills tween width back to full
Verify the merge animation (4→5) keeps elements centered under their token chips — no horizontal drift during the opacity crossfade
The legend (step 4), equation (step 5), and sidenote extras should fade in after the primary column animation completes
Test rapid forward/backward clicking through 3↔4↔5 — verify no stacking artifacts from interrupted tweens

name: Smooth Step 5↔6 — column consolidation
steps: Both steps use flipBuildColumns() — step 5 has separated green columns, step 6 adds hw-s35-at-6 class which collapses column gaps. Since DOM is rebuilt, the gap change is instant instead of animated
After Flip, GSAP-tween the column container's CSS gap property from step-5 spacing to step-6 spacing over 500ms, so columns visibly slide together
Token labels persist via tok-0..7 flip IDs — verify they move smoothly as gap collapses
Dimension labels ('T × d_model'), matrix border, and 'This is X' annotation text should enter with GSAP fade (opacity 0→1) + slight slide-up (y: 10→0) after the gap animation completes
For backward 6→5: GSAP-tween gap from step-6 spacing back to step-5 spacing. Dimension labels and matrix border fade out before gap expands
Verify the consolidation animation looks like columns physically merging into a single matrix object
Test in both themes — matrix border color differs between dark and light mode

name: Smooth Step 6↔7 — green→purple color tween + QKV entrance
steps: Both steps use flipBuildColumns() — step 7 passes cellVals: normCellVals and adds hw-s35-at-7 class. The green→purple color change and QKV weight matrix appearance are both instant on DOM rebuild
After Flip match, GSAP-tween cell text color from green values (#4ade80 or var(--green)) to purple values (#a78bfa or var(--purple)) over 500ms using gsap.to() on all .hw-s35-cell elements
GSAP-tween background tint from green to purple on the column pill containers (.hw-s35-green elements) — use backgroundColor or a CSS custom property tween

Cell VALUE text should update during the color tween — start showing green numbers, crossfade to purple numbers at the midpoint (set old values initially, swap textContent at 250ms into the 500ms tween)
QKV weight matrices row (hw-norm-qkv-row or equivalent) enters with GSAP slide-up (y: 30→0) + staggered fade-in per matrix card (stagger: 0.1, duration: 0.4) — W_Q first, then W_K, then W_V
The normalization arrow/label enters with fade before QKV cards appear
For backward 7→6: purple→green color tween reverses, cell values revert, QKV cards slide down and fade out
Verify cell VALUE text updates (green numbers → purple numbers) are visible and not jarring

name: Smooth Step 7↔8 — layout reorganization with element tracking
steps: This is the biggest layout change: step 7 has vertical layout (normalized matrix + QKV below via flipBuildColumns) → step 8 has horizontal layout (input matrix left + multiplication right via renderStep8). Only tok-0..7 match across the transition

Add data-flip-id='input-matrix' to the normalized matrix CONTAINER in step 7 (the hw-s35-body or equivalent wrapper) AND to the input matrix wrapper in step 8 (hw-q8-mat-wrap) — so the matrix itself animates from center to left position
Add data-flip-id='wq-matrix' to the W_Q card in step 7's QKV row AND to the weight matrix in step 8 — so W_Q appears to move from the QKV row into the multiplication area
W_K and W_V should fade out via onLeave with duration 0.3 (verify they don't teleport or scale-shrink awkwardly)
The Q output matrix, dot operator symbol, and equals sign enter via onEnter with staggered fade-in (stagger: 0.05)
For backward 8→7: matrix animates from left back to center, W_Q returns from multiplication area to QKV row position, W_K and W_V fade back in via onEnter
This transition benefits from a slightly longer Flip duration (0.6-0.7s) due to the large layout shift
Verify the input matrix column pills match visually between step 7's purple pills and step 8's purple input columns — styles must be compatible for the Flip to look right

name: Smooth Step 8↔9↔10 — projection carousel
steps: Input matrix already matches via tok-0..7 across steps 8-10. The issues are: weight matrices swap instantly, output matrices appear/disappear without visual connection

Add data-flip-id='weight-matrix' to the weight matrix element in steps 8, 9, and 10 so it Flips in place — only the label and color change. After Flip, tween the weight matrix background/border color from step N's color to step N+1's color over 400ms
Add data-flip-id='output-matrix' to the Q output matrix in step 8 and the V output matrix in step 9 — so Q output Flips to V output position (or stays in place if positions match)
After Flip for 8→9, tween the output matrix header label from 'Q' to 'V' styling (color change), and tween output column colors from blue (Q) to pink (V) over 400ms
Step 9→10: Q/V output stack clears with fade. K output matrix + transpose section enter with staggered onEnter. Weight matrix color tweens from pink (W_V) to orange (W_K)
For backward transitions: reverse color tweens and entrance/exit animations for all three directions (10→9, 9→8)
Verify the weight matrix color tween makes it clear the same matrix slot is being reused with different learned weights
Test rapid cycling through 8↔9↔10 — verify cascade animations (per-token highlights) don't conflict with Flip tweens

name: Smooth Step 10→11 — K^T persistence into QK^T
steps: The K^T matrix from step 10's transpose section should persist as the K^T operand in step 11's QK^T multiplication layout
Add matching data-flip-id='kt-wrap' on the K^T container in step 10 (the transpose result wrapper) — step 11 already has this on the K^T operand, verify it matches exactly
K^T should Flip from its step-10 position (below/beside K in the transpose section) to its step-11 position (right side of the Q × K^T multiplication row)
Step 10's input matrix, W_K weight matrix, K output, and transpose arrow should fade out via onLeave — verify timing so they don't disappear before K^T starts moving
Step 11's Q matrix, dot operator (·), and result scores grid should enter via onEnter with stagger (Q first, then operator, then result grid)
For backward 11→10: K^T Flips back from step-11 position to step-10 position. Step 10's full projection layout rebuilds around it with cascade entrance animation
Verify the K^T movement animation makes it visually obvious that the same transposed key matrix is being carried forward into the dot product
Test both directions and verify the dimension labels (d_head × T) persist on the K^T element during the transition
